Ph.D. Degree Program
General Requirements
Students accepted into our Ph.D. program must demonstrate excellent graduate coursework performance, pass the Qualifying Exam, and demonstrate satisfactory progress in research during the first four semesters of their graduate study at Ohio State.
After passing the Qualifying Exam, the student's progress will be monitored by his or her faculty advisor. In accordance with The Ohio State University Graduate School policy, each student must pass a Candidacy Examination after having completed all required course work. Upon passing the Candidacy Examination, the student becomes a Ph.D. Candidate. The Ph.D. Candidate will then complete a satisfactory Ph.D. Dissertation and Oral Examination.
Additional requirements, such as residency and guidelines for preparation of the dissertation, and time limits are explained in the Graduate School Handbook. In general, a student may complete the Ph.D degree in five years, depending on the research area and if he/she already has a Master's of Science (M.S.) degree.
Credit Hour Requirements
80 credit hours are required for the Ph.D. degree. The credits are broken down into the following categories:
Core Courses
The total core course requirements are 15 credit hours as listed below. These courses and the material prerequisite to them must be mastered by all PhD degree students. A student may be excused from any of the following required courses if an equivalent course was taken for the MS degree at another
university. In order to be excused from one of the core courses, the student must submit a detailed description of the course, including the syllabus, details of where and when it was taken, and a copy of the transcript showing a grade for this course, to the Graduate Program Coordinator and Graduate Studies
Committee Chair. The GSC will typically consult with the faculty member who most recently taught the course to review these materials and then decide whether or not to allow the student to substitute the transfer course in place of the related OSU course.
CBE 8801 (3 cr) - Analysis of CBE Problems
CBE 8808 (3 cr) - Advanced Thermodynamics I
CBE 8812 (3 cr) - Advanced Kinetics I
CBE 8815 (3 cr) - Advanced Transport
CBE 8781 (2 cr) - Research Communications in CBE
Chem 6781 (1 cr) - Laboratory Safety
Advanced Coursework
The minimum requirement is 12 credit hours. Graduate level courses in chemical and biomolecular engineering or other scientific, mathematics or engineering disciplines are to be selected to fit the candidate's goals with the consent of the advisor.
Research and Related Requirements
At least 53 credit hours of research (CBE 8999) are required. Each student should match with an appropriate research advisor and select a research topic in collaboration with the advisor by the end of the first semester of work in the PhD program. Research credits in further semesters should be taken with that
advisor. It is the student’s responsibility to follow the departmental matching procedures to find a mutually agreeable match and to proactively address any issues with the match with the advisor and/or the GSC. A satisfactory dissertation, as judged by the advisor and the student’s examination committee under the GSH rules, must be submitted as one of the requirements for the PhD degree.
In addition, PhD students are required to register for research seminar each Autumn and Spring semester and are required to learn about teaching and communication during a course associated with two instructional assistantship experiences as described further below. Students can petition the Graduate Program Coordinator and chair of the GSC for exceptions or modifications to these policies, which can be made by the GSC based on the circumstances (for instance, students’ requirement to register for seminar may be waived for them to attend an elective at the same time). Provided the student is concurrently making adequate progress towards their dissertation research, determined for this purpose by satisfactory grades in CBE 8999, seminar and instructional experience credits can count towards the research credit requirements. Pre-candidacy students should generally register for enough research credit hours to make a total of 18 credit hours in Autumn and Spring semesters.
Transferring Masters Degree Credits
If a student has a Master's Degree in Chemical Engineering from another university, they may transfer it as 30 semester hours of credit. This will change the requirements for the following: Advanced coursework from 12 to 6 credits and Research Credits from 53 credits to 29 credits.
Teaching Requirements Requirements
A crucial PhD program educational objective in CBE is intellectual leadership skills. Intellectual leadership involves more than the generation of knowledge through research, but also its transfer through effective communication. Some of these skills can be most effectively developed by “hands-on” practice
communicating with more junior students about technical content. This leads to the requirement that graduate students serve as instructional assistants and reflect on their learning and skills development in a concomitant course, during at least 2 different semesters. In addition to making an invaluable contribution
to the undergraduate teaching mission of the CBE program, these required mentored teaching experiences help ensure that PhD students are able to teach what they have learned and are able to critically judge the technical communications and ideas of others.
The specifics of the requirements are as follows.
At the end of their first year, PhD students will complete the University’s graduate teaching orientation to become eligible to serve as instructional assistants (IAs) or graduate teaching associates (GTAs).
PhD students in their second year or later will be assigned, in 2 different semesters during their PhD studies, to serve as an IA in a specific course by the Graduate Program Coordinator. During each of these semesters, IAs will assist with the assigned course and enroll in 3 credits of the instructional practice (teaching practicum) course in CBE. This course requires the student to perform adequately in their instructional assistantship and reflect on their experience. Note that IAs are not appointed as Graduate Teaching Assistants (GTA) nor paid additional compensation.
A GTA experience generally can count towards the IA requirement; this must be approved by the GSC.
The average workload for an IA should not exceed 9 hr/week.

There are three main exams that must be completed in order to complete the doctoral degree.
